record.title: Eurobarometer finds 42% of surveyed EU SMEs and mid-caps currently use AI or algorithmic management
record.summary: The European Commission published Flash Eurobarometer 578 on October 14, 2026, reporting on telephone interviews with 12,826 heads of privately owned small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps with 1–749 employees across all 27 EU member states. In the survey’s combined AI-or-algorithmic-management categories, 42% reported current use (12% extensive and 30% limited or experimental), 21% planned use, 35% had no plan, and 2% did not know. The infographic also reports that 75% expected these tools to improve job quality. These are company-reported survey responses: the measure combines AI with algorithmic management, and does not establish independently verified deployment, productivity, or workforce effects.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The European Commission published Flash Eurobarometer 578 on AI and algorithmic management in European SMEs and mid-caps on October 14, 2026. Its infographic says fieldwork ran March 20–April 13, 2026, using telephone interviews with 12,826 respondents drawn from privately owned SMEs and mid-caps with 1–749 employees across all 27 EU member states.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For the combined category of AI or algorithmic management, the survey reports 42% current use (12% extensive, 30% limited or experimental), 21% planning to use, 35% with no plan, and 2% unsure.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The infographic reports that 75% of surveyed companies expect AI and algorithmic management to improve job quality. It also says 90% of companies using the tools keep people in charge of decisions: 38% report human decisions without AI, 52% AI suggestions with human decisions, 7% AI decisions with possible human review, and 2% fully automated decisions without human review; 1% did not know.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The infographic lists investment costs (50%), uncertainty about legal or regulatory rules (49%), and lack of internal expertise (48%) as the most common barriers to AI or algorithmic-management adoption.

evidence_gaps.description: The report infographic does not expose the full questionnaire, country-level sample allocation and weighting, response rate, sampling error, or microdata in the inspected artifact.
The headline category combines AI with algorithmic management and combines extensive use with limited or experimental use; it cannot isolate AI adoption or production deployment.
Surveyed expectations of productivity, job quality, and adoption plans are not realized outcomes.

brief.importance_rationale: If representative, the survey would show meaningful current and planned use of AI or algorithmic management among businesses across all 27 EU states, informing both adoption assumptions and workplace policy. The score is bounded because categories combine AI with other automated management tools, answers are self-reported, and realized productivity, employment, and job-quality outcomes were not measured.
limitations: The reported use categories combine artificial intelligence with algorithmic management; the infographic does not isolate AI-only uptake.
Results are telephone-interview responses from company heads, not independently verified system inventories, audited purchase or usage records, or representative measurements of all EU employers.

The infographic gives the target population, date range, and interview count but not the complete questionnaire, weighting, response rate, sampling error, or microdata; the linked Eurobarometer survey-detail page loaded only as a client-side shell in this review.
Plans and expectations are not realized deployment, productivity changes, job-quality outcomes, employment effects, or causal impacts.

technical.claimed_result: Flash Eurobarometer 578 reports that 42% of surveyed EU SMEs and mid-caps currently use AI or algorithmic management, 21% plan to, 35% have no plan, and 2% are unsure; the currently using group includes 12% extensive and 30% limited or experimental use.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Commission published the survey and infographic, which report telephone fieldwork with 12,826 privately owned SME and mid-cap respondents across 27 EU countries. The adoption and expectation figures remain self-reported survey results.
technical.implementation_status: Survey respondents reported use or plans; no independent deployment verification was conducted.
technical.mechanism: The survey asked company heads about their use and plans for AI and algorithmic management in workplace tasks, decision-making, and job quality. The infographic separates current use into extensive and limited/experimental categories.
technical.regime: Privately owned EU SMEs and mid-caps with 1–749 employees; telephone fieldwork from March 20 to April 13, 2026. Categories combine AI and algorithmic management.
technical.strongest_baseline: This is a cross-sectional survey; no prior matched measurement or same-firm change estimate is provided in the reviewed infographic.

brief.title: Eurobarometer finds 42% of surveyed EU SMEs and mid-caps currently use AI or algorithmic management
brief.why_it_matters: This offers a new cross-EU snapshot of reported workplace adoption, near-term plans, and employer expectations among privately owned SMEs and mid-caps. The split between current use, experimental or limited use, and planned use can inform adoption assumptions and labor-policy discussion. The categories combine AI with algorithmic management, however, and the survey does not measure installed systems, productivity, or realized effects on workers.
